topics.topic: Define PublicationMark.marked_at time source, representation, and read timing/count
questions: From which time source is `marked_at` obtained, is it stored as offset-free UTC or an offset-aware datetime, and how many readings does one mark operation take?
Which authority supplies the instant written to `PublicationMark.marked_at` when a new mark is created?
In which representation must `PublicationMark.marked_at` be stored: offset-free UTC, offset-aware UTC, local time, or another representation?
How many time-source readings does a mark operation take, at what point is the reading taken, and do replayed or refused mark operations read it?

quotes:
1. The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

2. Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

3. The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.
judgement.why: A7 specifies the clock authority, exactly one read and its position, which refused and replayed marks read it, and the offset-free UTC representation assigned to marked_at.

topics.topic: Specify lexical parsing and normalization of settings values, including integer port syntax
questions: Which environment-variable spellings count as a whole-number port—for example, are a leading plus sign, leading zeroes or surrounding whitespace accepted?
What exact lexical decoding and normalization must the settings module apply, including whitespace, empty values, path expansion, enum names versus enum values, and integer syntax?

quotes:
Each run setting is a row of the start-up table that only the runtime settings module of SPEC_STANDARD 6.11
reads, into a field of the settings object; that module decides how a value is read.
judgement.why: Exact lexical decoding, normalization, integer syntax and accepted textual forms are input-format and field-decoding details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Decide whether INV-04 tests must assert offset-free UTC datetime representation
questions: Must this test explicitly assert that every resulting datetime is UTC without an offset, rather than merely representing the expected instant in UTC?

quotes: INV-04: camera times with an offset, without one, implausible or absent give the expected UTC value.
judgement.why: The Required-tests wording does not explicitly require checking the offset-free representation, but that wording is unchanged in the closed and current A2 texts and the A8 change did not make the omission newly relevant.

topics.topic: Decide whether photo modification time is read once and reused during preparation
questions: Must one preparation operation read the file modification time exactly once and reuse that same instant for camera-time plausibility checks and for the fallback photo moment?

quotes: _read_source_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST open entry once, relative to the folder descriptor, for reading only, without blocking and without following a link, and judge the opened object before reading it: one that is not a regular file MUST raise Rejected with the NOT_A_REGULAR_FILE member of = models.PlacementFailure, and a failure to open, inspect or read it MUST raise Rejected with the UNREADABLE_FILE member. It MUST read from the start until the end of the file or one byte past the imported MAX_SOURCE_BYTES constant, whichever comes first, raise Rejected with the TOO_LARGE member when that byte is reached, and otherwise return every byte read together with the status of the opened file taken before reading; the file MUST be closed on every path and never opened again.

_observed: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST judge the rejection orders of A1 in their order: a file whose listed size in info says it holds no byte is rejected with the EMPTY member of = models.ObservationReason and one whose listed size is above the imported MAX_SOURCE_BYTES constant with the TOO_LARGE member, both before the file is opened; then it MUST call _read_source_bytes once, and a Rejected it raises is rejected with the reason of the row of the imported OBSERVATION_FAILURES constant whose failure is its reason, no bytes read with the EMPTY member and _signature_format returning None with the UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT member. A rejected SourceFile carries the REJECTED member of = models.ScanStatus, the given name, the listed size, the time _modified_at gives for info, no source id and no bytes; otherwise it MUST return a SourceFile with the READY member of = models.ScanStatus, the lowercase hexadecimal digest of the imported sha256 of the bytes as source_id, their length as size and the time _modified_at gives for the status of the read, together with those bytes.

_photo_moment: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the EXIF of the first frame of image once, a reading that fails counting as no EXIF, giving each tag value to _parse_exif_moment only when it is a string and None otherwise, and return the first moment _parse_exif_moment gives, judged against modified and read in zone, for the EXIF DateTimeOriginal tag of the Exif directory with its OffsetTimeOriginal tag, then for the EXIF DateTime tag of the first directory with no offset, paired with the EXIF member of = models.DateSource; when neither gives one it MUST return modified unchanged with the FILE_MODIFIED member of = models.DateSource. It MUST NOT read the service clock.

_place: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] MUST call the imported prepare_photo with raw, the modified of source and the timezone of context, then the imported store_image with its content, then the imported build_publication, and write with the imported write_placement a PhotoPlacement of the project id and source id, the name of source, the reference store_image returned, the lowercase hexadecimal digest of the imported sha256 of the stored bytes and their length, the imported STORED_MEDIA_TYPE constant as media_type, the date_source of the prepared photo and the publication, returning that placement; an exception raised by any of these calls MUST pass to the caller unchanged.
judgement.why: The State 7 notes capture modification metadata from the opened file, carry that single modified value into preparation, and use the same value for both plausibility checks and fallback.

topics.topic: Define the lower port threshold as an imported typed policy constant
questions: The lower port threshold must become a data-provider constant named as `the imported X constant`, with its typed value added to the policy-values table.

topics.topic: Require enum member names instead of value-only references
questions: Replace each value-only reference with the emitted member name beside `= models.RefusalCode`, optionally retaining the value as a parenthetical supplement.
Name the TOO_LARGE member of = models.PlacementFailure instead of referring to the member only by its value `too_large`.

topics.topic: Specify startup behavior for an invalid or out-of-range port setting
questions: What must startup do when the port setting is present but cannot be read as such a number or is outside this range?

quotes: A missing required setting or a value of the wrong form ends the start.
A port above 65535, an unknown time zone or an invalid connections file ends the start.
judgement.why: The public-operation contract says malformed setting values and ports above the maximum end startup rather than receiving the absent-value default.
